subject.title: [Feature]: Track data provenance across session boundaries for persistent state

question: What provenance contract should OpenClaw expose for durable state writes and later reads before plugins and security policy can rely on it?
rationale: The source gap is clear, but the permanent API, storage schema, plugin visibility boundary, and read-time trust policy are product and security decisions.

options.title: Define a core provenance contract
options.body: Keep this issue as the canonical durable-provenance design item and specify structured tool-output, write-time, and read-time provenance before implementation.

options.title: Scope memory first
options.body: Start with durable memory source refs and lineage, then revisit files, cron, preferences, and config after the memory contract proves out.

options.title: Fold into the security umbrella
options.body: Let the broader persistent-taint/security architecture issue own this and keep this thread as supporting context only.

recommendation.title: Define a core provenance contract
recommendation.body: Keep this issue as the canonical durable-provenance design item and specify structured tool-output, write-time, and read-time provenance before implementation.

likelyOwner.reason: This owner has the strongest combined history across input provenance, memory host boundaries, and recent central files touched by the proposed contract.
